concept: One vague comment gets taken apart and rebuilt, piece by piece, on one board in one office. The same two colleagues and the same presentation run from the hook to the payoff, and the opening frame returns changed: the nod now has something behind it.

story.metaphor: A comment is a thing built from three pieces on one board: an observed action, its effect, one next step.
story.setting: One small cartoon office meeting room after a talk: a projector screen on the right wall, a meeting table front left, a wall calendar on the back wall, a whiteboard on the side wall, and the viewer's own desk in POV.
story.arc: Warm nod, nothing changes (b01, b02); the same comment is rebuilt on the board (b04 to b07); the viewer picks and checks (b08 to b11); the opening room returns and this time she opens differently (b12).

parts.what: The small meeting room after the talk, drawn once: ctx.scenery room with a surface2 wall and field2 floor, a projector screen on the right wall, a meeting table edge front left (muted top, field2 front), a wall calendar slot on the back wall, and 4 to 5 seated muted audience extras (ctx.crowd) in two rows facing the screen. No accent furniture, no shelf. The screen shows either a dense text-wall slide (grey hand-lettered lines, no accent) or a single slide reading 'Decision' in hand lettering. The audience is either looking down at phones (small surface2 phone shapes in hand) or heads up toward the screen.
A paper wall calendar with an accent3 header band and one hand-lettered page that flips over its top ring from 'This week' to 'Next week' (Patrick Hand, weight 400, ink on surface). Pins in muted.

The 'Natural presenter' chat bubble (seed bubble: chat), surface fill, ink outline, Nunito body text 'Natural presenter', with a small muted heart beside the words. Never in the accent. States: spoken (full size with a tail toward Maya), held (only the muted heart, small, resting in her hands), small_grey (shrunk to 40 %, greyed, no tail).

The meeting-room whiteboard: a surface board with an ink outline and a muted tray, holding three slots in one row (left, middle, right), each slot a dashed muted outline 440 x 170 when empty. A narrow side window on its left edge can open onto the meeting room (the room_cutaway). The same slot geometry is reused as the draft card on the viewer's desk (state draft: a paper card 1200 wide, three empty slots, a blinking ink cursor in slot 1).

The three comment pieces as tiles that fit the board slots, each with a tilted stamp label (seed label: stamp) beside it in Patrick Hand: tile 1 'Read the slides aloud' stamped 'Observed action', tile 2 'Room looked at phones' stamped 'Effect', tile 3 'Open with one decision' stamped 'Next step'. Tile text Nunito body, ink. States per tile: muted (field2 fill), accent (the accent fill with field text, only one tile at a time), empty (dashed outline, stamp in muted). State joined: the three tiles locked edge to edge inside one chat bubble outline, read left to right as one sentence, stamps underneath in order.

kit.notes: People are never kit parts: Maya is ctx.character('Maya','maya',...), Theo is kit.peep(...,'man',...,{cloth:'cloth2',skin:2}) with literals in every beat. The templates in b04, b06, b08, b09 and b10 cannot use the kit; they mirror its wording (same tile phrases and stamp names) so the comment reads as the same thing.

stations.note: Station A: the hook and the payoff. Theo screen left at the table, Maya screen right by the projector screen, calendar on the back wall.

stations.zone: the whiteboard on the meeting-room side wall
stations.note: Station B, to the right of A: forward in the lesson. The comment is rebuilt here; the quiz and the checklist come back to it.
Station C, below the board: deeper, the viewer's own work. Reached by a camera move down.

devices.what: The whiteboard on the meeting-room wall, held as one station. The old bubble is pinned on it, then the three comment pieces fill its slots while the layout stays put. Hold the layout and change its state.

The three comment pieces as tiles with a stamp label (Observed action, Effect, Next step). Each keeps its slot position and stamp all lesson. The piece being named carries the one saturated accent; the others drop to muted tints. They return as checklist rows, as empty draft slots and in the payoff bubble.

The 'natural presenter' chat bubble with a muted heart: spoken in the hook, held in her hands as a feeling, pinned to the board, shown small for contrast and returning as quiz option 1. It never takes the accent.
A wall calendar that flips to 'Next week' (stepped time). In the hook it shows nothing changed; in the payoff it shows the change. b06 names next week in the page line.
The audience in the meeting room: small muted extras, first looking down at phones, later looking up. Seen through the board's side window in b05 and as the before and after in b12.
Join material: a paper page turn at chapter boundaries on the warm paper ground, plus one hard cut at the quiz turn. Gradual continue joins inside sections.

Back to the calm, productive board at rest energy.

value_script.accent: the rebuilt comment bubble, then her decision slide
value_script.why: A lift at the close. The opening frame returns brighter, and the accent finally appears in the office scene itself.

scenes.rationale: The misconception has to be watched happening: the warm nod, then the calendar flip, then the same slide-reading pose. Change over time is the point.

design.treatment: Wide on the meeting room (kit meeting_room, state slide_text_wall, phones_down later). Theo as a seated peep bust behind the table edge, screen left, facing right. design.why_motion: The point is a sequence in time: comment, nod, a week passes, nothing changed. A still frame cannot show that nothing changed.

design.treatment: Medium on the comment_board (kit, three slots in a row). Tile 1 'Read the slides aloud' sits muted in slot 1 with its 'Observed action' stamp. A narrow side window on the board's left edge opens onto the meeting_room (kit, phones_down). Tile 2 takes the accent; slot 3 stays empty.
design.why_motion: The order is the teaching: first the room reacts, then the words for that reaction land, so the effect reads as observed rather than guessed.

design.treatment: A slight pull back on the comment_board. design.why_motion: Separate pieces joining into one sentence is the claim: the motion of locking together says 'one comment', and the in-order flood says the order.
